results.title: Modular valuation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, is a modular valuation when $f(X) + f(Y) = f(X \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y)$ for all $X, Y \in L$.

results.title: Strictly positive valuation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ is strictly positive when $f(X) > 0$ for every $X \in L$.

results.title: Gilbert condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, satisfies the Gilbert condition when $f(X \vee Z) + f(Z \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y) \ge f(X \wedge Z) + f(Z \wedge Y) + f(X \vee Y \vee Z)$ for all $X, Y, Z \in L$.

results.title: Generalized Jaccard distance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, the Jaccard distance of $X, Y \in L$ is $d_f(X, Y) = 1 - f(X \wedge Y) / f(X \vee Y)$.

results.title: Characterization of the Gilbert condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ satisfies the Gilbert condition if and only if $f$ is a modular valuation and is monotone, that is, $X \le Y$ implies $f(X) \le f(Y)$.

results.title: Jaccard distance as a single quotient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$. Then for all $X, Y \in L$ the Jaccard distance of $X$ and $Y$ with respect to $f$ is $d_f(X, Y) = (f(X \vee Y) - f(X \wedge Y)) / f(X \vee Y)$.

results.title: Jaccard triangle inequality under the Gilbert condition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$ that satisfies the Gilbert condition, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.

results.title: Triangle inequality for the generalized Jaccard distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive, monotone modular valuation on a lattice $L$, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.

results.title: Left-orderable multiplication
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multiplication of a set $B$ is left-orderable when there is a strict total order $<$ on $B$ that is invariant under left multiplication: for all $a, b, c \in B$, if $b < c$ then $a b < a c$.

results.title: Left-orderable addition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The addition of a set $B$ is left-orderable when there is a strict total order $<$ on $B$ that is invariant under left addition: for all $a, b, c \in B$, if $b < c$ then $a + b < a + c$.

results.title: Hessian matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the Hessian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is the $n \times n$ real matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0} \frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0} f(x + s e_i + t e_j)$, where $e_1, \dots, e_n$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$.

results.title: Entries of the Hessian matrix

results.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and indices $i, j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Hessian matrix of $f$ at $x$ is $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0} \frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0} f(x + s e_i + t e_j)$, where $e_1, \dots, e_n$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$: differentiate first along $e_j$, then along $e_i$.

results.title: Hessian entries as second Fréchet derivatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable and let $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. For all indices $i, j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the Hessian matrix of $f$ at $x$ equals $D(Df)(x)(e_i)(e_j)$, the derivative of the Fréchet derivative $Df$ at $x$ in the direction $e_i$, applied to $e_j$, where $e_1, \dots, e_n$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Symmetry of the Hessian
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Second-derivative test, necessary condition

results.title: Dense clause
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A clause is a finite list of slots, where slot $j$ records how the variable $x_j$ occurs: the slot is either empty (the variable is absent) or holds a Boolean $b$, meaning the literal $x_j = b$; so $b$ true gives $x_j$ and $b$ false gives $\lnot x_j$.

results.title: Dense CNF formula
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A CNF formula is a finite list of dense clauses, read as the conjunction of its clauses.

results.title: Satisfaction of a dense clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite bit sequence $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ satisfies a clause $c$ when there are an index $j$ and a Boolean $b$ such that slot $j$ of $c$ holds the literal $x_j = b$, $j < n$, and $a_j = b$. Variables $x_j$ with $j \ge n$ are unassigned and satisfy no literal.

results.title: Satisfaction of a dense CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite bit sequence $a$ satisfies a CNF formula $\varphi$ when $a$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.

results.title: Dense decoding with an accumulator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a bit string $w$ and the list $c$ of slots read so far for the current clause, stored in reverse order, the result is the CNF formula obtained by reading $w$ two bits at a time: $00$ outputs the current clause in reading order and continues with no slots read; $01$ adds an empty slot to the current clause; and $1s$, for a bit $s$, adds a slot holding the Boolean $\lnot s$, so $10$ adds a positive and $11$ a…

results.title: Dense decoding of CNF formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The CNF formula decoded from a bit string $w$ is the result of the accumulator decoding of $w$ started with no slots read for the current clause: $w$ is read two bits at a time, $00$ ends a clause, $01$ is an empty slot, $10$ a positive and $11$ a negative literal, and a trailing unterminated clause and a dangling odd bit are ignored.

results.title: Two-bit code of a slot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Slot $j$ of a dense clause is empty (variable $x_j$ is absent), holds the positive literal $x_j$, or holds the negative literal $\neg x_j$. Its code is $01$ when empty, $10$ for the positive literal and $11$ for the negative literal.

results.title: Dense encoding of a clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bit string encoding a clause is the concatenation of the two-bit codes of its slots, in order (empty slot $01$, positive literal $10$, negative literal $11$), followed by the terminator $00$.

results.title: Dense encoding of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dense encoding of a CNF formula $\varphi$ is the bit string obtained by concatenating, in order, the encodings of the clauses of $\varphi$, where a clause is encoded as the two-bit codes of its slots followed by the terminator $00$.

results.title: Decoding inverts the dense encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, decoding the bit string that encodes $\varphi$ gives back $\varphi$. In particular, every CNF formula is the decoding of some bit string.

results.title: Dense CNF-SAT
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A bit string $w$ belongs to dense CNF-SAT when the CNF formula obtained by decoding $w$ in the dense clause encoding is satisfiable, that is, some assignment (a list of booleans) satisfies every clause of the decoded formula.

results.caption: Definition
